purpose: Human-reviewed semantic deduplication; no distinct clinical instructions are removed.

omissions.reason: The retained flow separately distinguishes chemical, thermal, penetrating/open-globe, and blunt/superficial injury and gives their different care.
Blunt and penetrating eye injury applicability is expressly retained in the overview.
Chemical and thermal eye injury applicability is expressly retained in the overview.
High-velocity injury, impaled object and visual loss are retained in the urgent-red-flag overview; suspected open globe is retained in the EMT action.
Life threats and associated trauma take priority in the retained overview/EMT actions, with associated head/facial/systemic injury and no transport delay in AEMT care.

The known/strongly suspected chemically contaminated open-globe exception, noncontact shield, urgent ophthalmology/Poison Help/Medical Control consultation, and no delay for hypothetical rupture are repeated verbatim in EMT care.
Thermal cooling/irrigation with room-temperature water or saline and eye protection are retained in the flow; no ice, ointment or pressure remains in warnings.

The blunt-injury flow retains shielding when globe injury is suspected; focused assessment retains all listed visual/pupil/hyphema/diplopia/movement/proptosis findings; associated head/facial trauma and no pressure/patch are retained.
The express Medical Control restriction on ketamine for suspected penetrating/open-globe trauma is retained in the Paramedic actions.
EMT open-globe care already prohibits instilling medication into a suspected penetrating/open-globe injury; this applies to topical anesthetic too.

Immediate water/saline irrigation without waiting for ideal fluid and the distinction between hypothetical rupture and known/strongly suspected contaminated open globe are retained together in EMT care.
Nonpressure rigid shielding, prohibition on pressure, and no eye patching are retained; the pearl adds explanation but no different clinical action.
Visual-acuity assessment when feasible and prohibition on delaying time-sensitive transport to complete testing are retained in EMT care.
Hemorrhage control, indicated pelvic stabilization, hypothermia prevention, rapid transport and not delaying definitive hemorrhage control are all retained in provider actions.
Abdominal/pelvic symptoms, wound and evisceration/impalement findings, seatbelt sign and unstable perfusion findings are retained in the focused/high-risk assessment.
Suspected pelvic fracture/pain/deformity and all listed genitourinary, rectal/vaginal, voiding and neurologic red flags are retained in the flow and assessment.

AEMT actions retain IV/IO without transport delay, adult blood-unavailable warmed-crystalloid perfusion strategy, 80–90 non-TBI endpoint, ≥110 including age70 TBI target, normal saline, no permissive hypotension and BP reassessment; medication note retains respiratory/perfusion reassessment.

The complete Paramedic-only trauma TXA eligibility, ≤3h timing, adult 1g/10min OR 2g/20min (100mg/min maximum), stocked preparation verification, no automatic repeat, topical-use distinction, documentation and duplicate-dose handoff instructions are retained in the Paramedic action.
Authorized analgesia/antiemetic treatment, NPO, preservation of mental-status/perfusion assessment and rapid transport, and serial reassessment are retained.

The >approximately20-week displacement/tilt rule and trauma compatibility remain in Paramedic care; maternal priority, early pregnancy notification and trauma/obstetric-capable destination remain in retained pregnancy and warning sections.
TXA must not delay transport or definitive hemorrhage control is retained in the complete Paramedic TXA action.
Injury/dose/time documentation, duplicate-dose prevention handoff and no inference from topical indications are retained in the complete Paramedic TXA action.

No impaled-object removal/evisceration reduction, no direct pressure on exposed viscera and no blind abdominal packing are retained in provider and detailed treatment instructions, including the separate lifesaving removal exception elsewhere.
Pelvic pain/high-risk mechanism or shock prompting stabilization and avoidance of repeated manual pelvic testing are retained; the pearl adds rationale rather than a different action.
Correct binder positioning and rapid transport without delaying for repeated pelvic assessment/procedures are retained.
The same approximately20-week pregnancy threshold, manual left displacement or left tilt, and spinal/trauma compatibility are retained in Paramedic actions.

The retained contraindication requires complete perfusion assessment and BP trend rather than one reading, the assessment lists trends, and indications explicitly recognize inadequate perfusion regardless of BP.
Cause treatment, perfusion support, avoiding harmful indiscriminate fluids and early definitive-care transport are all retained in provider actions and warnings.
Exact duplicate of retained large-volume crystalloid warning.
Exact duplicate of retained suspected-TBI permissive-hypotension warning.
Manual BP confirmation when feasible and correct cuff size are retained in EMT care.
The retained warning explicitly states normal mental status/GCS15 does not exclude shock.
Treating immediately reversible causes through linked protocols is retained in Paramedic care.
The same ECG indications (ischemia, dysrhythmia, pulmonary embolism, cardiogenic shock) are retained with acquisition and interpretation in Paramedic care.
Waveform capnography during assisted ventilation and when clinically useful in severe shock is retained in Paramedic care.
Universal care, airway/ventilation, clinically indicated oxygen, condition-specific positioning and heat-loss prevention are retained in EMT care.
Immediate hemorrhage control, identification of internal/external bleeding and rapid transport for time-critical causes are retained.

The identical nonhemorrhagic/no-overload 500mL IV/IO rule remains in AEMT care; medication note and trend assessment retain lung sounds, work of breathing, perfusion, mental status, BP/MAP, heart rate and optional EtCO2 reassessment.
Exact250mL aliquot strategy and heart/renal/liver/cardiogenic/overload indications with reassessment are retained in AEMT care.

The complete blood-unavailable non-TBI warmed-crystalloid perfusion/80–90SBP strategy, reassessment and limited volume remain in AEMT care; hemorrhage control and rapid definitive-care transport remain in EMT care.

Exact same adultTBI≥110including70, no permissive hypotension, avoid hypoxemia/excess fluid, normal saline and frequent/post-treatment BP reassessment are retained in the TBI special-population section.

Paramedic vasopressor initiation for persistent inadequate perfusion after appropriate fluid or earlier when further fluid is contraindicated, with continuous ECG/frequent BP monitoring, is retained in Paramedic care.
The same epinephrine indication, 2–10mcg/min IV/IO dose and adequate-perfusion/MAP≥65 titration target are retained in Paramedic care.
Early transport/receiving notification and no delay for repeated IV attempts, fluid-target completion or BP normalization are retained.
Paramedic norepinephrine authority and persistent-shock/fluid-contraindication conditions are retained in Paramedic care.
Exact ECG/frequent BP monitoring requirement is retained in Paramedic care.
Epinephrine as Paramedic alternative when norepinephrine is unavailable or significant bradycardia accompanies shock is retained in Paramedic care.
Exact ECG/frequent BP monitoring requirement is retained in Paramedic care.
The250mL heart/renal/liver/overload-risk aliquot is retained in AEMT care; the retained fluid-stop rule includes pulmonary edema, worsening respiratory status and lack of fluid responsiveness.
The approximately20-week pregnancy threshold, left displacement/lateral positioning when feasible and AO03 link are retained in the more complete pregnancy treatment step.
The renal-failure emergencies and access complications are listed in the retained indications; the infection/peritonitis-to-sepsis flow retains the sepsis concern.
Access protection, early unstable hyperkalemia recognition, and treatment without waiting for laboratory confirmation remain in provider actions and assessment.

Immediate ABC/perfusion care, access protection and linked emergency care including infection/sepsis are retained; this sentence adds no dose or threshold.

The calcium-gluconate row retains initial1.5–3g IV, maximum3g/episode, and no repeat without specific Medical Control confirmation of cumulative dose.
